   "new_text": "### The gate\n\n**The gate** (`problem.prevalence`) **carries `event`, not `question`.** Code asks it as *In {window}, did you\n{event}?* and, straight after, *In {window}, on how many {unit} did you {event}?* Write only what happened, as a\nclause that completes both frames: the base form, the person implied — *work out why your baby was crying*.\n\n**The gate is answered *Yes* or *No*, and they cover everyone** — a person who cannot recall it happening answers *No*.\nWrite no escape and no options for it: code shows the story's chips after a *Yes*, beside the story box, never beside\n*Yes* and *No*.\n\n**The gate asks the problem, not the routine.** Write `event` from `problem`: the same problem, said to them in the\nwords `context.actor_plural` use for it, spelled right — the base form, *you* and *your* for *they* and *their*,\nshorter only by dropping joining words -- never the thing the act is done to, nor the other party. Never write it from\n`context.circumstance`. `problem` *had to sort site photos and type up the daily log by hand after the site walk* is\nasked *type up the daily log after your site walk*, never *put your photos and notes into the daily log*: everyone\ndoes that, so nobody could answer *No*. Only where `problem` is `null`, write what went wrong in\n`context.circumstance`, never the routine itself.\n\n**Keep what went wrong.** Where `problem` says a thing was missed, lost, left unanswered, late, wrong or redone, `event`\nsays that word too, in their words: it is the part a person without the problem answers *No* to. `problem` *calls went\nunanswered and guests were lost* is asked *a booking call to you go unanswered*, never *take a booking call*: a call\ncoming in is what every one of them meets, so nobody could answer *No*.\n\n**Add nothing to `problem`.** No place, time, step, tool or condition that `problem` does not say (*after leaving the\nsite*, *at home*, *once the shift was over*): an added word narrows who answers *Yes*, so a person with the problem\nthe founder counted must answer *No*. Every word of `event` is a word of `problem`, its plain form, or *you* and\n*your*.\n\n**Test it**, both ways: one of `context.actor_plural` who did the same work in the window with nothing going wrong truly\nanswers *No* — else it is the routine: put back what went wrong. One who had the problem as `problem` says it, wherever\nand however it happened, truly answers *Yes* — else a word was added or narrowed: take it out.\n\n- **One thing that happened**, so that *No* means one thing: never two events joined by *or* or *and*, never a clause\n  where *No* could mean *it did not happen* or *I did it another way*. Keep the one part of `problem` the person had to\n  do or put up with, the setting and the condition `problem` itself gives, and nothing it does not — every word that\n  narrows who had it is the founder's, so no more and no fewer answer *Yes* than the founder counted.\n- **Seen on a given {unit} or not**: never a lasting state (money left sitting), never what happens every working day\n  anyway (a call coming in), no cause packed in (*because*, *from*, *so that*).\n- **The act whole**, so a hard time still answers *Yes*; never how long, how much or how hard (*hours*, *too long*).\n- **The verb first**, the person implied — or, when what went wrong happened to them, **its subject first, in the\n  second person**: `problem` *a payroll went out with an error* is asked *your payroll go out with an error in it*,\n  never *run your payroll*.\n- **The verb says the act, never a verdict on it**, the way it was done or what might have been: none of *idle*,\n  *sitting*, *still*, *stay*, *have to*, *fail to*, *waste*, *struggle*, *by hand*, *manually*, *could have*, *would\n  have*, *more than it could*, *better*.\n- **Short**: framed, each of the two questions is at most 20 words: the clause fits *In {window}, on how many {unit}\n  did you {event}?* in 20 spoken words.\n- No digit and no number word; none of *last*, *past*, *recent*, *recently*, *ago*, *today*, *yesterday*, *week*,\n  *month*, *year*, *day*, *night*, *shift* or *cycle*, nor the window's own unit; one clause, no question mark; it\n  never begins with *in*, *how many*, *did you*, *out of* or *do you think*.\n- **About the most recent real time**, never a habit: never *usually*, *typically*, *normally*, *in general*,\n  *generally*, *on average* or *most of the time*.\n- **No founder value**: not a number of theirs and not a phrase of their answers (*Most*, *Nearly all*).\n- **It never mentions the idea.** None of *app*, *apps*, *platform*, *dashboard*, *portal*, *plugin*, *api*, *saas*,\n  *website*, *algorithm*, *device*, nor any form of *automate*, *integrate* or *sync*, and none of the idea's own\n  terms.",
   "why": "Both failing gates drifted from the founder's problem in opposite directions: Fresco's added a setting the problem never gave (after leaving the jobsite), so a super who typed the log up in the trailer had to say No, and Codyco's dropped what went wrong (unanswered), leaving the circumstance every agent meets, so No had nobody. The edit adds two rules, keep the word that says what went wrong and add nothing the problem does not say, and turns the test into a two-way check, so a person without the problem says No and a person with it says Yes wherever it happened; it also tightens the setting clause to the setting the problem itself gives. These rules read only `problem` and `context.actor_plural`, so they hold for every trade and every study, keep the gate's fixed Yes and No with no escape as the card requires, and leave the chips after a Yes untouched.",

then the clause says so plainly.\n- The label's people and place stay; the words are `context.actor_plural`'s.\n- The label is at most 16 words; the clause, framed, is still at most 20.\n\n**Adoption friction is the step in base form, as the stranger's own act**: *upload your last 12 months of pay\nregisters, once* -- what they set up, learn, hand over, check or do differently.
